description: A master clock with eight outputs, each firing on a different multiple of the clock pulse

params.text: Starts and stops the clock; it comes up stopped, and stopping it zeroes the step count and drops every output to 0V
Sets the tempo, 30 to 360 BPM; the clock pulses twice per beat

outputs.text: Sends a 10ms pulse at 10V each time the run switch is moved to on
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V on every clock pulse
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V on every second clock pulse
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V whenever the step count divides by 3; the count wraps every eight pulses, so two gaps of three pulses are followed by one of two
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V on every fourth clock pulse
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V whenever the step count divides by 5; the count wraps every eight pulses, so it fires twice in eight, five pulses apart and then three
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V whenever the step count divides by 6; the count wraps every eight pulses, so it fires twice in eight, six pulses apart and then two
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V whenever the step count divides by 7; the count wraps every eight pulses, so it fires twice in eight, seven pulses apart and then one
Fires a 10ms pulse at 10V on every eighth clock pulse

notes: the clock is stopped when the module is first placed, and the run switch has to be moved to on before anything comes out
a Ktick placed immediately to the right is fed by this clock and sends its four division factors back here
the maker's README lists a reset input for this module; there is no input jack on the panel, and the reset pulse comes out of the Rst output when the clock is started
